newsitem.title: CANADA: Nurses in Province of Alberta vote to strike.
newsitem.headline: Nurses in Province of Alberta vote to strike.

text.p: Alberta's registered nurses have voted in favour of a strike that could come as early as Thursday night, according to a report from the Canadian Press news agency.
Eighty-five per cent of nurses who voted Tuesday supported a strike. Seventy-two per cent of the 10,500 union members voted.

Earlier in the day, hospital lobbies were filled with patients being sent home to be looked after by home-care nurses and families in anticipation of a strike. Regional health authorities cancelled all elective surgeries across Alberta.
Up to 800 people were scheduled for discharge in Calgary hospitals alone, and new mothers with uncomplicated births were to be asked to leave after six hours.
"It's a mandate we hope we never have to exercise," said union president Heather Smith. "Hopefullly it means there's going to be a deal."
The vote results were released as negotiators for the United Nurses of Alberta and the provincial health authorities continued contract negotiations.
The two sides were deadlocked over who should be in charge of hospital wards.
Nurses insist only registered nurses should be in supervisory roles, while the health authorities would like to have the flexibility to hire other health-care professionals to fill the jobs.
Smith also said late Tuesday the union is willing to accept the employer's offer of a wage increase of 7.25 percent over three years.

"The membership of this organisation has indicated all along that this is not a monetary issue; this is about patient care," said Smith. "We made movements in our positions at the table to ensure that that's what was reflected."
"The nurses have every right as far as I'm concerned. They're worked to death," said Hilda Steinberg, whose husband was sent home early to recover from a viral infection.
Joy Werner, a nurse in the Royal Alexandra's ophthalmology ward, said she was shocked that people who were scheduled for the most routine eye operations were told to go home.
"I was really upset because the employer knows that we're going to be here today and we've always given at least 48 hours notice before we strike," Werner said.
